sections.h2: Where is Chesapeake, Virginia, and how big is it?
sections.html:
Chesapeake is an independent city in the Hampton Roads area of southeastern Virginia. It borders Portsmouth and Norfolk to the north, Virginia Beach to the east, Suffolk to the west, and North Carolina's Currituck and Camden counties to the south.

The 2020 census counted 249,422 residents, making it the second most populous city in Virginia. By land area it is the second largest city in the state, with about 338.5 square miles of land and 12.4 square miles of water. Elevation is only 16 feet.

The modern city dates to 1963, when South Norfolk merged with what remained of Norfolk County, approved by referendum and authorized by the General Assembly. The Battle of Great Bridge was fought here on December 9, 1775.

sections.h2: What are Chesapeake's six boroughs and waterways?
sections.html:
The city is divided into six boroughs: South Norfolk, Butts Road, Deep Creek, Pleasant Grove, Western Branch and Washington. A house in each borough can feel very different, from dense older streets to large rural lots.

Water shapes the whole city. The northeastern part of the Great Dismal Swamp lies in Chesapeake, and the Great Dismal Swamp National Wildlife Refuge covers a large piece of it. The Atlantic Intracoastal Waterway passes through, along with the Western and Southern Branches of the Elizabeth River and the Dismal Swamp Canal, which runs parallel to U.S. Highway 17.

With an average elevation of 16 feet, much of the city sits low, so ask the city for the flood zone of your parcel before you list, particularly if the lot is near water.

sections.h2: What does the climate mean for a Chesapeake house?
sections.html:
Chesapeake has a humid subtropical climate, with hot, humid summers and mild to cool winters. Annual precipitation averages about 48.4 inches, and mean daily highs run from roughly 49.7 degrees in January to 88.7 in July.

Humidity matters for houses. Crawl space moisture, attic ventilation and air conditioning load are typical items a buyer's inspector will raise, and a house with deferred upkeep can show those problems quickly.

sections.h2: Who employs people in Chesapeake and how do roads connect the city?
sections.html:
The largest employers are the public schools (6,248), the City of Chesapeake (3,927), Chesapeake Regional Medical Center (2,038), Walmart (1,783) and Sentara Healthcare (1,478). Dollar Tree has its international headquarters here, and the Navy runs Northwest Annex and NALF Fentress.

  • Interstates: I-64 (part of the Hampton Roads Beltway), I-464 and I-664.
  • U.S. highways: 13, 17, 58 and 460.
  • Tolls: the Chesapeake Expressway on State Route 168, Veterans Bridge and Jordan Bridge.
  • Five movable bridges, which open an estimated 30,000 times a year.

Norfolk International Airport serves the city, and five railroads, including CSX and Norfolk Southern, run through it. A bridge opening can slow a commute, which is a detail buyers ask about.

sections.h2: When are Chesapeake real estate taxes due?
sections.html:
Chesapeake bills real estate tax in four quarterly payments, which is different from the two payment schedule most Virginia localities use. The Treasurer's due dates page lists the dates below, and says a date that falls on a weekend or holiday moves to the next business day.

PaymentDue date
1st quarterSeptember 30
2nd quarterDecember 31
3rd quarterMarch 31
4th quarterJune 5
Stormwater, 1st halfJune 5
Stormwater, 2nd halfDecember 31
Tax relief filingBy May 15

The page says penalty and interest are applied as required by state and city code if a payment is not postmarked or received by the deadline, and it gives no percentages. The ceilings in Code of Virginia 58.1-3916 are 10 percent for the property tax penalty and 10 percent a year for interest, so ask the Treasurer what the city actually charges.

sections.h2: What is the Chesapeake tax rate and stormwater fee?
sections.html:
The city lists a real estate tax rate of $1.01 per $100 of assessed value for fiscal year 2026 to 2027, which includes $0.01 for mosquito control. The stormwater fee for a single residence is $136.20 a year, paid in two installments of $68.10.

Under City Code Section 26-372, the stormwater fee is payable by the owner of the billed parcel. That matters for a sale, because a bill that is unpaid when you list may be there when you close.

The Treasurer's office can be emailed at paytax@cityofchesapeake.net, and the city main line is 757-382-2489. The address is 306 Cedar Road, Chesapeake, VA 23322.

sections.h2: How does the Chesapeake Real Estate Assessor set and change values?
sections.html:
Chesapeake values property as of January 1, and new values take effect July 1. Owners whose value changed are mailed a notice, and for the current cycle those notices go out on or before March 1, 2027.

New construction, additions and demolitions are picked up through supplemental bills, with valuation changes captured on October 1, January 1, April 1 and July 1. A teardown or an addition done before listing can therefore change the bill during the year.

The Assessor's office is at 306 Cedar Road, 4th Floor, with phone 757-382-6235 and email assessor@cityofchesapeake.net. A free property search is available at chesapeake.civ.quest, while the city's paid tax information subscription costs $1,100 a year or $100 a month.

sections.h2: How can you appeal a Chesapeake assessment?
sections.html:
Chesapeake gives owners three routes, and you can use more than one. You may contact the Assessor to schedule a property review, apply to the Board of Equalization, or petition the Circuit Court.

  • The Board application must show the property is valued above fair market value, or that the assessment is not applied uniformly, or does not follow accepted appraisal standards or Virginia law.
  • The city posts an Appeal Process guide, instructions for filing, and an application as PDFs.
  • The page says time limits apply but does not state them, so ask the Assessor's office before you plan.

For owners over 65 or disabled, the city runs tax relief through the Commissioner of the Revenue at 757-382-6455, option 4. Applications run from January 1 through May 15, and the city listed relief of 100 percent for household income up to $25,000 in fiscal year 2025. Check the current limits, because they are listed by year.

sections.h2: What should Chesapeake sellers watch for at closing?
sections.html:
Chesapeake sellers should confirm four things: the current quarter's real estate tax, the stormwater fee, any land use enrollment and the recordation costs. The city's own page notes that Virginia does not allow title transfer when delinquent taxes are paid through a tax lien sale, so back taxes can complicate a sale if they are left too long.

If the land is in the use value program, the minimums are 5 acres for agricultural, horticultural and open space land and 20 acres for forest land. A change in use or a rezoning at the owner's request can trigger rollback taxes covering the current year and the five most recent complete tax years, plus simple interest.

Virginia's grantor tax is 50 cents per $500 of value under 58.1-802. Cash Home Buyers can buy a Chesapeake house as is, including one with overdue tax, and the Treasurer's payoff can come out of the proceeds.

faqs.q: When are Chesapeake real estate taxes due?
faqs.a: In four quarterly payments: September 30, December 31, March 31 and June 5. A date on a weekend or holiday moves to the next business day.

faqs.q: What is the Chesapeake real estate tax rate?
faqs.a: The city lists $1.01 per $100 of assessed value for fiscal year 2026 to 2027, which includes $0.01 for mosquito control.

faqs.q: How do I appeal a Chesapeake assessment?
faqs.a: Contact the Real Estate Assessor at 757-382-6235 for a property review, apply to the Board of Equalization, or petition the Circuit Court. You can use more than one route.

faqs.q: What is the Chesapeake stormwater fee?
faqs.a: For a single residence the city lists $136.20 a year, due in two installments of $68.10 on June 5 and December 31. The owner of the billed parcel pays it.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Chesapeake house with unpaid taxes?
faqs.a: Yes, the balance is normally settled from the proceeds at closing. Ask the Treasurer for a payoff that matches your closing date.
